[quote=the_crystalline_empire;61631368][b]July 27, 2028: The Northern Dilemma[/b]

Haakon Strømm stood in his office once again, a newspaper tossed in evident fury upon his desk, the Montfleurois had broken their neutrality. This was an unprecedented move, Haakon had assumed, perhaps foolishly, that the Montfleurois would fail to come to a consensus regarding action against Rosenmarkke, fearing international repercussions, and a damage of tradition. However, this was not the case.

He had just met with Begren to discuss the matter on the home-front, Begren had made great successes in Mittlemarkke, leveraging the loyalty of the Duc there to ensure that any movement towards re-unifcation was stomped out. Begrens move to stop the naval defection two days earlier had been genius in Haakons mind. However, Begren still didnt have enough men, or resources, in order to conduct a full national operation, many SCSID units had been sovietised during the war, and Haakon suspected that many had silently joined the side of the unionists.

Haakon had been unwell since his rant against the generals on July 5, he knew that there was planning against him going on and he knew that the pool of loyalists to the regime was shrinking day by day. As a result he had shifted his trust onto Begren and his successes, however, the two had their differences.

Begren for instance was demanding more resources and more centralisation, Haakon was unable to produce or decree such a matter due to the dissent in the various regions, not to mention Haakon was terrified of making such demands to his own council due to questions of loyalty. 

The door to the office opened,  and generals Kieffe and sse entered the room, nodding as Haakon motioned for them to sit.

Gentlemen, it is good to see you, he intoned smoothly.

As to you, they echoed.

Let us get to business, continued Haakon as he sat down behind the desk.

I am sure you are aware Montfleur has revoked their neutrality, he stated.

Yes, replied sse.

And you are aware that this is an attempt to invade us, to justify an invasion? Asked Haakon.

We regret to admit that we didnt know of this intel, replied Kieffe.

Begren has informed me of this, replied Haakon.

Kieffe frowned at the name of the fresh headed SCSID director, he was too impulsive, too rash, and Kieffe believed that Begren had been feeding Haakon information to drive his political aims.

Now, I would take this as a declaration of war, a violation of our sovereignty, and with centralisation of the army continuing successfully, and the officers being purged, I see it as the next stage of the revolution to overcome the Montfleurois threat, continued Haakon.

I see, replied sse carefully.

So, I intend to be declaring war on Montfleur, said Haakon, We shall complete what the revolution started,

sse coughed politely, If I may speak sir, Rosenmarkke is not politically ready for such a war, even as we speak, Begren has failed to crush or stop the secessionist movement in Thýven or Knygta, 

Haakon frowned, Begren tells me he plans on arresting the duc of both those areas today,

It was Kieffes turn to reply, This is highly irregular and you risk making a martyr out of the two ducs

That will drive the unionists out of their holes, smiled Haakon.

I will be releasing a war declaration tomorrow, I expect full coordinating power with Begren, that is all,

As Kieffe and sse walked out of the office and down the marble halls of the legislative building they muttered amongst themselves.

Hes gone mad, intoned Kieffe in a low tone.

Hes got that little worm whispering in his ear, replied sse with a shake of his head as they stopped at the elevator, the doors dinged and they stepped inside.

I understand that he is trying to restore the order of things, but, it seems like he is speedrunning our dissolution, scoffed sse as they reached the first floor and stepped out into the foyer.

Kieffe frowned, What are the optics if someone attempted a coup on him? he asked.

Tsk, not here, not here, replied sse looking around the lobby as they stepped out onto the street.

Kieffe and sse walked to their car which was waiting on the curb, the two men got in.

Regarding your suggestion, stated sse, We can look into it, but, with this Begren fellow, I dont trust him, he continued, putting the key into the ignition.

Neith Kieffe got cut off as the ignition started and the car burst into a fireball, killing both men instantly as the bomb that had been planted in the hood of the car activated. 

[b]War and the Security State: Preserving the Nation Through Disruption[/b]

There is no doubt that war and the SCSID go hand in hand, the SCSID was formed during a time period of cold war as a mechanism to prevent internal war within the state, while permitting Rosenmarkke to inflict a silent external war on enemy nations.

It is in this that the SCSID acts as an internal and external chameleon, holding one name but many functions.

   - General Harven Røsjln (Speech: January 6, 1978)[/quote]

[b]July 28, 2028: War[/b]

My fellow citizens,

Yesterday the Montfleurois terrorists brutally executed the brightest commanders of our armed forces, killing them with a weapon of street warfare, a car bomb. 

For the past several months, the Montfleurois regime has sought to bring down our Strømmist Republic, and we have nobly taken provocation after provocations! 

It has become clear that Montfleur is not a neutral country, but a terrorist regime! As a result I call upon all citizens to mobilize and prepare to complete the next stage of our great revolution, the vanquishing of our enemy, Montfleur!

[b]July 29, 2028: War II[/b]

Mrjkanlwyth stood in the old baptist church before the men of the association, weary lines etched into his face. The men were not triumphant as they had been earlier in the month, they were sombre, awaking to the reality that unfolded before them. The true cost of freedom had revealed itself.

Gentlemen, intoned Lambeau, rising from his pew and looking at his compatriots, We always knew this day was coming, the regime would never agree to fall on its knees so quickly, he nodded, The cost of freedom is severe, but, if we should perish, our blood will lay the path for our children to make a better land and to teach their children to live in a better land, 

Mr. Zedde nodded, It is lamentable, he replied, But it is necessary, 

Arise you people of the revolution! Sang Meternisse quietly.

the hour of glory has arrived, sang another.

Against us tyranny, the bloody standard is raised, sang the rest of the men.

Lets March, lets March, so impure blood waters our furrows! Sang all the men as they stomped their canes in unison, rising to salute the Rosenmarkket flag that hung on the left of the sanctuary.

Gentlemen, go home to your families tonight, for tomorrow I command you to cross that river! Declared Mjrkanlwyth to claps and cheers.

[b]A grim reality[/b]

The national assembly sat quietly as Henri stood once again at the podium, the declaration of war had been delivered by the Rosenmarkket ambassador to Montfleur that morning, although the media had already covered it since the day prior.

My fellow friends,

It is clear now, that there is no turning back with Rosenmarkke, there can be no turning back, we have entered into the path of history, our next actions will determine how the world order continues. 

Gentlemen and ladies, the objectives of this war are purely on self defense terms, the Rosenmarkket state has already sealed its fate with its reckless acts, and we will defend ourselves to the very last drop of the sacred blood.

Rosenmarkke is already collapsing, there can be nothing we can do to either follow it through or to stop it, that is all.

Henri nodded and walked out of the hall, which remained silent as murmures filled the room, uneasy, unsteady.

Henri walked through the back hallways of the Palais de Congress, his guards ten meters behind him, Henri needed to be alone.


The Treasury delivered a statement earlier this morning, that Gold and Silver shipments will resume as of Wednesday, June 21st.
This follows a dramatic surge in the price of gold and silver, surging 25% during the Wuloosyan-Rosenmarkke War, which endangered traffic traversing the Pale Strait. Monitoring of the situation by the Arelian Navy has concluded, drawing a conclusion that it is capable of protecting shipping traffic passing through.

The Arelian 3rd Fleet will protect shipments through the Strait, with our ships expected to arrive in Aurestia later this evening. The US Treasurer will lead the effort, clearing the way.

[b]August 1, 2028: Soldiers[/b]

[spoiler]The first order had arrived before sunrise, awakening the commander of the 3rd Thývenic Infantry Brigade, it told him to go westward. Then at breakfast another command came, ordering him to stay put, this one from a different official, then another telling him to go southward to join the forces massing in Mittlemarkke.

Iseg Radwell now sat in his office peering out the window where the soldiers, trucks, and other vehicles were being readied to deploy to wherever the last order had stated.

He hadnt surmised yet the worst case scenario, and that was the total collapse of any form of hierarchy, he had already known of four units within Thýven which had apparently abandoned their posts and gone home once the declaration of war had been issued, he already knew that some within his own brigade were plotting a similar manner.

However, Iseg had vowed to serve Rosenmarkke thirty years prior, and while the regime was insane, the protection of the citizens was paramount regardless of the state.

As he watched out of the window blinds a young soldier walked in, a staffer really, he held an envelope. 

Give it, stated Iseg not turning from the window as the soldier walked forward and handed it to him, nodding he dismissed the fellow and opened the letter, his brow furrowed immediately.

[i]NOTICE: All contact with Knygta and Deyn has ceased, it is believed that local command centers are being hijacked, standby for further order.[/i]

Dropping the letter on his desk he moved out of the office, walking briskly down the hall and into the command yard, I want a full review he snapped at one of the officers, who began ordering the troops to get into formation for a review.

Where are the trucks? Asked Iseg looking for the convoy trucks.

They left, replied a soldier who was standing by.

Where?! Demanded Iseg.

The soldier shrugged.

The yard soon filled with troops and movement, headcounts had begun, they were missing several soldiers and a few officers.

Sir, said a voice, Iseg spun around as he saw the radio operator rush up to him.

What?! Demanded Isag, Spit it out!

The radios are being jammed, we cannot establish communications with central command, 

Iseg frowned, something had gone terribly wrong, Can we identify where the jamming is coming from? 

No sir, most likely within the region though, 

Iseg pursed his lips, turned to one of his officers and shook his head, How many do we have? He asked.

We are missing about 1/4th sir, replied the officer.

Iseg nodded, Send them back to their posts, the barracks, whatever, we will wait for a more conclusive set of orders, before walking back to his office.

[b]Haakon Strømm: Spirals[/b]

Were losing the islands, intoned Iosef Begren grimly.

You assured me they were secure, replied Haakon quietly.

We underestimated the local ground movement, and our overreach, replied Begren.

Haakon nodded, We shouldve arrested the duc, 

Are the Montfleurois aware? He asked.

I am not sure, replied Begren, The SCSID just doesnt have the manpower right now, replied Begren.

Haakon sighed, Shut down the internet, jam all non-essential radio comms, close the borders, 

That would make matters far worse sir, replied Begren.

Do it, I dont give a d-mn, the central army will handle it, waved Haakon.

Begren nodded, and left the room.

[b]Montfleur: A flurry of info[/b]

Your majesty, the Gendarme has stopped a convoy of trucks from Rosenmarkke attempting to cross our border, the soldiers surrendered upon reaching the border and are in custody of the state, began General Louis De Funes, head of the Gendarme.

Henri nodded as Eleonore took notes, leaning back in his chair, How are the islands, he asked looking at the head of General Security Directorate, Peter Jalouse.

Intel suggests that the duc has cut off communications, local militias have been activated, and there seems to be plans to storm one of the remaining bases on the island, replied Jalouse.

Henri pursed his lips and nodded again, Good, any word from the regime?

None, sir, replied Jalouse, Although there seems to be some decohesion in the forces in Thýven, 

Sir, theyve cut the internet, piped up one of the aides as they looked up from an telecom pad that had been laid on the table.

Henri smiled, It seems the regime is afraid, how long do you give the state Peter? 

Sir, at this rate, if Knygta and Deyn secedes as they alerted us, and does so without issue, we expect Westmarkke, Thýven, and Belgarde to follow within the next few days to weeks, he replied.

Will we need boots in Rosenmarkke? asked Henri of Louis.

Only once the first regions secede and request union, replied the aged general.

Could we put boots on the islands? asked Henri.

The general shook his head, Not without suppressing the abilities of the ground forces of the mainland, they still have submarine capabilities, and due to how rapidly the situation is forming, well wed have to wait days to a week perhaps to deploy a formal defensive/offensive force, 

Henri frowned and looked at Eleonore, What is your take? 

Eleonore looked up from her notepad, Belgarde we could get troops in, I am aware that our largest base of support is there, and the commander of the regional forces has actually been in contact with me already, he is good friends with the duc. But as for a naval expedition, its several thousand kilometers around the coast.

What is the situation in Belgarde, director? Asked Henri of Peter.

Last we checked, stable, they are expected to be a staging ground for any forces, replied Peter.

Eleonore, would the assembly support an immediate unionisation of Belgarde? If we can legally integrate them into the state as soon as possible, then any troop movements would constitute an invasion of our sovereign territory, 

Eleonore nodded, Its hard to say, wed have to assure them that Belgarde is doing this of their own will,

Phones are down, stated the aide once more.

Sir, stated another aide, stepping into the room, The Bojerries has arrived,

Henri smiled, Ah good, lunch for all of us, we need it, he stood up and clapped. 

After a few moments of discussions a tray of fast food was brought into the room, filling the room with the smell of fried chicken, another tray of Nuka Kola cans was also brought in and, Henri began handing them out as the officers and aides filled their paper plates with food.

See, unlike the Rosenmarkket leadership, we here in Montfleur like a good time, even in situations of dire importance, stated Henri, opening his vicodin bottle and popping a pill in, screwing the lid tight.

[b]August 2, 2028: Secession[/b]

Albert Iverkjthing stood quietly in his bedroom, the morning sunlight peeking through the closed curtains that hung on his window. Comms had been cut with the government and militias had been raised, the government had made haste to cut the internet, the phones, however, thanks to the redundancy of the government, they had failed to remember the emergency telegraph lines which had been laid across the country in the event all major communications had been cut by an enemy. Now, Knygta and Deyn was using it against them to relay orders to the various defecting groups on the mainland.

Albert had unwillingly become the leader of the secessionist movement, he rose from the bed, stretched, and began to dress himself, looking in the mirror he frowned, what would come next? Could the state recover from such an action, would Haakon unleash the army against the islands?

He had been assured that the navy was weak, incapable, and that any response would be weak, after all, the war with Wuloosya had ravaged the major infrastructure of the islands, but, concerns had risen that the SCSID would be able to launch a precision attack to end the movement instantaneously.

He left the room, went downstairs, and left the house, stepping onto the street, he noted how quiet the city was, once the busiest city in Rosenmarkke, the economic hub, the streets had gone silent. He would have to walk, the electricity had gone out and the subway wasnt working.

As he walked down the street, passerbys stopped and stared, pointing at him in hushed whispers, he noted civilians and militia members dressed in camo raided from outpost stores and surplus stores as well as attics and basements across the island. These militia members wore a distinctive blue and yellow armband.

Arriving at the office of the duc of Knygta and Deyn, he looked out the window onto the large square that faced the office, a crowd had begun to gather, he was expected to formally declare secession in an hour to the whole world.

Withdrawing from his desk the crumpled speech he had prepared, he read through it, smoothing its edges out. After an hour, the time came, his aide walked in, nodded, and two members of the militia moved to open the doors that led to the balcony, Albert stepped out.

The roar of the crowd hit him like a wave, cheers and clapping filled the area as signs and flags were waved, some pro-unionist, some independence, and some just there. He waved to the crowd and stepped forward to the microphones that had been set up.

My people and foreigners and workers and all members of this nation, welcome,

I stand before you today, on this momentous occasion, to declare to the world, to the regime, and to all people who tune their ears to listen. Freedom has won, freedom will win, freedom will forever win. 

From the earliest days of these islands, we have prided ourselves in our rugged individualism, our culture, and our republican heritage. We have stood as the heart of Rosenmarkke since before Rosenmarkke existed. 

And thus, as we see the nation crumbling day by day, we must take matters into our own hands. We must fight against the forces of tyranny that assail themselves against our homes, our families, our workplaces. We must fight against the forces of despotism that threaten to undermine the global order, and destroy our individuality. We must fight against Strømmism and individualistic politics. We must fight.

It is with this declaration, that we will fight, on the beaches, in the sea, we will fight until there is no longer a fight left in us. 

Knygta and Deyn, I declare you free!

The crowd roared with support as the last words echoed over the crowd, the church bells began to ring in the city as music began to play and a group of militiamen rushed to tear down the Rosenmarkket flag from the pole that stood in the center of the square. [/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]The Other Ministry[/b]][b]The Other Ministry[/b]

In Sallacher politics, there exists a set of ministers that take up the task of administering the matters of state. These ministers, grouped up into a Council of Ministers, form the cabinet structure of Sallach, and are typically expected to function transparently and visibly, with government mandates on the use of publicly-accessible websites detailing each and every transaction and plan implemented by such ministers with the approval of the princely government.

However, as was typically the case in politics, Sallach did not fully conform to matters of transparency, and many things are retained in total darkess to safeguard both the institution of monarchy and the safety of the Sallacher nation. One of these so-called "shadow organizations" was [i]L'autre ministère du prince[/i] ("The Prince's Other Ministry"), a hidden section of the Council of Ministers dedicated to espionage and surveillance, whose legacy extends back centuries to the Maréchaussée of the Ancien Regime.

As it so happens, this Other Ministry had been scheduled meet with the Regenerator government at Palais Bleu on the Rosenmarkke case.

"It's pandemonium" said L'autre, setting down a hefty report of events. "This no longer concerns matters of neutrality and ethics, monsieur. We are witnessing the collapse of the Rosenmarkket state in real-time, if we intend to act, and we must, we need to do it now, or else we may very well wake up to a new world that has been swallowed up in the fires of the EDU and the Socintern."

"I've already received word from the Montfleurois government that they were on top of things." said the Comte d'Ardelay, crossing his arms into a quiet sigh. "We have nothing to gain from foreign entanglement in affairs that do not concern us. Sallach has thrived for nearly a century by avoiding these entanglements, I'm not about to destroy this by joining now."

"You don't understand, ministre en chef. Right now, we are witnessing socialists preparing to invade socialists!" L'autre countered, angrily slamming his fist against the table. "The Montfleurois cannot be trusted. If we allow the Montfleurois to exert full and uncontested control over the declining Rosenmarkket state, tomorrow we will see SummitONE operatives propping up the same soviets in the fatherland. We must gain leverage over all actors and seize territory now, now while the situation remains fully in our favor!"

"And how certain exactly is L'autre ministère that events will play out as they've prescribed?"

"Citharo is practically licking their lips at the prospect of subsuming our fatherland into the Socintern."

"Citharo is busy with its own affairs in Dhornaper."

"Citharo is an international. Just because all of its major eyes are in Shamat doesn't mean that its Sanguinian and Gythenan operatives haven't been keeping up to date in the White Straits. If we allow communism to take root, and it has already taken root in a more moderate form, it shall fester horrifically, for communism itself is a wound, and it shall infect our blood and destroy us. Then, we will be dead, unless you act now. We cannot have red banners flying over our banner, even if they have been useful in shielding us from the excesses brought on by the EDU."

At that,  L'autre quietly leaned back, having contented himself with having presented the fullest extent of his arguments. He turned around, leaving the Regenerators with his report on the table, its map of the White Straits staring ominously back at them. The Comte d'Ardelay thought for a little while.[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Operation Fusilier[/b]][b]Operation Fusilier[/b]

Sallach has not fought a war with any power on Erene since the conclusion of the Framta Crisis. Because of this, the country has not maintained a proper, standardized armed forces. Instead, the country made use of a special organization called the Corps des Gendarmes et Volontaires ("Corps of Gendarmes and Volunteers"), a volunteer-only formation that served as the country's official military and national police force.

Uniquely among the nations of Erene, the Corps continues to appoint its officers in the feudal style. Lower officers are typically meritocratic, but the highest echelons remain reserved for the nobility, who function as Sallach's professional military caste. While novel, this has left the Corps essentially deprived of technically-capable leadership, with much of its functions reduced to engaging with civilian and cultural duties.

Still, the nation had a substantial military inventory for its size, and was by all accounts considered a militarily-capable power, with a good network of military staff and modernized training regimens. The Princely Palatine Guard, which serves as the honor guard of Sallach, is further noted for maintaining the country's only active tank company. There were 11,000 gendarmes and volunteers in active service within the country, 8,000 of whom were considered fully ready to be deployed at any time.

After some deliberations within the Defense Committee of the Sallacher Senate, it was decided that command over the operation was to fall into the hands of Lt. Gen. Charles Augustin de Estienne-Porcéan de La Driennais, a second cousin of Prince Guillaume and one of the higher-ranking Regenerator senators in government. While reluctant to actually take command, the Count of Porcéan would be assured of the "relative simplicity" of the operation, and would begin an invasion of Rosenmarkke along South Belgarde.

"Operation Fusilier", as it was called, would be a fairly limited affair despite its grand scope. With an infantry division of around 6,000 men, Porcéan was ordered to use a column of tanks and APCs supplied by the Palatine Guard to capture the airfields controlled by the Belgardian soviets, which the Sallacher Air Wing hopes to use in order to ferry along special forces to strategic locations pending the main Montfleurois invasion that was to come.

Politically, Sallacher forces hoped to eliminate any soviets encountered along the path through South Belgarde and to supplant these forces with localized "committees of correspondence" that could administer the resulting territories "without the need for unwanted adherence to pollutive ideologies", though Porcéan would be warned to avoid unnecessary firefights with soviet forces that might try to resist dissolution, with the Regenerator Government fearing retaliation from SummitONE or the wider Socintern.[/spoiler]
